answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: an agent must lock a bond in a shared liquidity lagoon before it may trade. Think of the bond like an ancient relic whose provenance is public: anyone can verify it is real and unspent. A sybil attacker creating ten thousand fake identities must lock ten thousand bonds, paying real capital and losing the time funds sit idle, and fraud burns the bond. Meanwhile honest agents broadcast a reputation beacon of signed attestations, so peers trust bonded history, not free claims. Mass fakery becomes a capital loss rather than free spam.
